newsitem.title: GERMANY: German employers, IG Metall start talks in Berlin.
newsitem.headline: German employers, IG Metall start talks in Berlin.

text.p: Wage talks for around 60,000 engineering workers in the western part of Berlin started on Thursday, with the IG Metall union demanding an agreement matching a breakthrough accord reached in the state of Lower Saxony last week.

In addition to Lower Saxony, the engineering industry has already reached accords in North Rhine-Westphalia, Bavaria and southern Baden-Wuerttemberg. They all enshrine full sick pay alongside wage rises of 1.5 percent for 1997 and 2.5 percent for 1998.

The deals mean that the majority of Germany's 3.2 million engineering workers have achieved their goal of preventing the implementation in their sector of a new law allowing a 20 percent cut in pay during sickness.
Further talks have been set in other regions. IG Metall said talks covering more than 400,000 workers in the states of Hesse, Rhineland-Palatinate and Saarland are scheduled for December 18.
Talks will also be held for the northern part of the state of Baden-Wuerrtemberg and for the coastal region covering Schleswig-Holstein, Hamburg, Bremen and the northwestern part of Lower Saxony.
